decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm elbow-up approach to the left tube, lifting before pitching toward a top-down grasp; right arm stays home.
Advance left wrist above the left tube while aligning its fingers across the tube body; maintain elbow-up continuity.
Complete top-down alignment over the left tube and descend cautiously toward its body, still open.
Refine the left grasp using wrist view: small pitch and lateral compensation while lowering to tube-body height.
Center the tube between the left fingers with a small forward adjustment, then close on its body.
Lift the closed left grasp clear of the table with a slight retreat, checking tube retention before turning upright.
Tube is retained in the left fingers. Begin a slow upright rotation while moving toward the rack's left-side slot.
Continue the retained tube's gradual upright rotation and approach, keeping the left elbow configuration continuous.
Finish turning the left tube upright above the rack's left region, maintaining clearance before the insertion descent.
Lower the upright retained tube toward the left-front large opening, with a small rearward alignment correction.
Refine the left-front slot alignment from the calibrated rack image before inserting deeper; keep the grasp closed.
Insert the upright left tube slowly into the aligned large slot; keep the fingers closed until seated.
Retry the unexecuted lift and small backward slot-alignment correction with the right arm stationary.
The visible large opening is now beneath the tube tip. Lower vertically in small increments to seat it.
Release the left tube at the opening and withdraw gently to inspect whether it remains upright and seated.
The first tube stands released in its slot. Withdraw the left arm toward home while the right arm begins an elbow-up approach to the rear right tube.
Continue left-arm return and advance the right wrist over the rear tube, aligning its grip across the tube axis.
Bring the left arm home while finishing the right tube's top-down approach; stop above final grasp depth for wrist-view alignment.
Fine-center the rear right tube in the wrist view and lower to its body; finish settling the left arm at origin.
Align across the rear right tube with a small yaw correction, then close the right gripper on its body.
Lift the second tube clear with the right gripper closed, retreating slightly before turning it upright.
The second tube is retained. Begin its gradual upright rotation and move toward the rack's right-side opening.
Continue rotating the retained right tube upright while approaching its slot with clearance.
Finish making the second tube upright above the right-front large slot before descending.
Lower the upright second tube toward the right-front opening, making a small lateral alignment adjustment.
Insert the upright second tube vertically into the opening beneath it, keeping the grasp closed during descent.
The second tube appears to contact the rim. Lift clear, correct slightly inward and backward, and begin a cautious retry.
Lower the realigned second tube slowly to seating depth, monitoring for rim contact.
The second tube remains on an edge. Lift and make a small inward/backward correction, also reducing its apparent outward lean.
Make the final small seating descent and release the second tube into the opening, then inspect its unsupported position.
Withdraw the open right fingers to observe whether the released second tube settles upright in its slot.
The second tube tipped instead of seating. Clear the rack to reveal its resting position for a recovery grasp.
Clear the fallen tube and begin a top-down approach to the remaining front-right tube; the fallen tube will need recovery afterward.
Continue the right-arm top-down approach to the front tube with small continuous wrist rotations.
Finish the top-down wrist alignment above the front-right tube, stopping short of contact to refine the grasp.
Lower onto the front tube and match its slight tabletop tilt, preserving the tube's position between the open fingers.
Shift the right fingers from the cap toward the tube body and refine yaw for a centered grasp.
Close on the centered front tube and begin a short lift to verify retention.
The front tube is retained. Lift to safe clearance and begin rotating it upright toward the rack.
Carry the retained front tube toward the rack and gradually rotate it upright, maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Approach an empty central rack opening from the right workspace while continuing the tube's upright rotation.
Finish the upright orientation above the central large opening, staying within the right arm's workspace.
Lower the upright tube toward the central opening and correct its small apparent rightward offset before final insertion.
Lower slowly into the central opening with the right grasp closed, checking that the tube descends rather than sliding on a rim.
Complete a short seating descent at the central slot and release, allowing the tube to settle without continued gripper pressure.
The central tube now stands released in its opening. Withdraw upward and rightward to recover the remaining fallen tube.
Raise clear of the rack and begin reorienting the right wrist for the fallen tube's reversed cap direction.
Approach above the fallen tube at safe height while continuing the wrist reorientation in small increments.
Continue the gradual recovery-grasp orientation above the fallen tube, keeping clearance from the two seated tubes.
Continue turning toward a top-down recovery grasp of the fallen tube, preserving joint continuity and clearance.
